name: Install Claude Code
tryIt: Run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
description: Install Claude Code on your machine. This is where it all begins — one command and you're ready to start building with AI.

name: Create a New Project
tryIt: Try saying: 'Create a new project with Vite and React'
description: Set up a fresh project directory. This is your blank canvas — every design-to-code journey starts here.

name: Describe and Build
tryIt: Try saying: 'Build a landing page with a hero section, feature cards, and a signup form'
description: Tell Claude what you want in plain language and watch it write the code. This is the core skill — describe your vision, get working software.

name: Preview in Browser
tryIt: Try saying: 'Start the dev server so I can see my app in the browser'
description: Start a local server so you can preview your work in a browser in real-time. See changes instantly as Claude builds your UI.

name: Use Screenshots for Feedback
tryIt: Give Claude a screenshot and tell it what to fix, or ask it what needs to be fixed.
description: Take a screenshot of your running app (Ctrl+Cmd+Shift+4) and paste it into your Claude window (Cmd+V in Claude app, Ctrl+V in the terminal). The most natural way to give feedback — just show it what needs fixing.

name: Iterate on Styling
tryIt: Try saying: 'Make the header bigger, add more padding, and change the accent color to blue'
description: Tell Claude to tweak colors, spacing, fonts, and layout. This is the bread and butter of working with Claude — describe what you want changed and watch it update the code in real time.

name: Change Your Claude Model
tryIt: Type /model in Claude Code to switch models, or try saying: 'Use Opus for this task'
description: Switch between Claude models like Sonnet and Opus to balance speed and capability. Use a fast model for quick edits and a powerful one when you need deep reasoning or complex builds.

name: Set Up GitHub
tryIt: Try saying: 'Set up a GitHub repo for this project and push the code'
description: Connect your project to GitHub for version control. This protects your work and lets you collaborate with engineers on their terms.

name: Clone a Branch — BHR Template
tryIt: Try saying: 'Clone the BHR frontend repo and get it running locally'
description: Clone the BHR frontend repository from GitHub and set it up on your machine. Your starting point for working on the real product codebase.

name: Create a Branch
tryIt: Try saying: 'Create a new branch called feature/redesign'
description: Create a separate branch to work on without affecting the main code. Essential for safe experimentation — you can always throw it away.

name: Commit and Push
tryIt: Try saying: 'Commit my changes and push to GitHub'
description: Save your work with a git commit and push it to GitHub. This is how you preserve your progress and share changes with your team.

name: Connect Figma MCP
tryIt: Share a Figma link and say: 'Look at this design'
description: Link Figma directly to Claude Code so it can see your actual design files — not just descriptions of them. This is the bridge between design and code.

name: Add to an Existing Screen
tryIt: Share a Figma component and say: 'Add this sidebar to the existing dashboard page'
description: Use a Figma design to add a new component or section to a page that already exists in code. The most common real-world design handoff — incremental changes, not greenfield builds.

name: Build a New Page from Figma
tryIt: Share a Figma link and say: 'Build this screen exactly as designed'
description: Give Claude a Figma link and have it generate a complete new page from scratch. Go from a design file to working code in minutes.

name: Use Playwright MCP
tryIt: Try saying: 'Take a screenshot of my app and compare it to the Figma design'
description: Use browser automation to navigate your running app, take screenshots, and compare them to your Figma designs. The design QA loop — refine until it's pixel-perfect.

name: Edit CLAUDE.md
tryIt: Try saying: 'Create a CLAUDE.md that tells Claude to use Tailwind and keep code simple'
description: Customize how Claude behaves in your project by editing its instructions file. Set your preferences, conventions, and constraints so Claude codes the way you want.

name: Use Claude's Plan Mode
tryIt: Try saying: 'Plan how you'd implement a settings page before building it'
description: Ask Claude to plan before it builds. Plan mode explores your codebase and proposes an approach before writing any code — perfect for complex features where you want to review the strategy first.

name: Create a Skill
tryIt: Try saying: 'Create a /component slash command that generates a React component from a description'
description: Build a custom slash command that packages a complex workflow into a single action. Your own personalized Claude superpower.

name: Generate Mockups
tryIt: Try saying: 'Generate 3 different layout options for a dashboard as a single HTML file with a way to switch between them'
description: Ask Claude to generate multiple HTML mockup variations for a single idea. Rapidly explore different layouts, styles, and approaches before committing to one direction.

name: Deploy to URL
tryIt: Try saying: 'Help me deploy this project to Vercel or Netlify so I can share the link'
description: Ship your project to the internet so anyone can see it. Share a real, clickable URL with stakeholders — not just a screenshot.

name: Run Multiple Instances of Claude
tryIt: Open two terminals, run 'claude' in each, and give them different tasks at the same time
description: Open multiple terminal tabs each running Claude Code on different tasks simultaneously. Parallelize your workflow — one instance builds the frontend while another sets up the backend.

name: Create a Chatbot
tryIt: Try saying: 'Build a chatbot that uses the Anthropic API with streaming responses'
description: Build a project that uses an AI API key, like a chatbot. Learn how real AI-powered features connect under the hood.
